solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Uncomfortable proximity in stifling billets

parts.note: stifling weather is close, airless and oppressive
billets are soldiers' lodgings, their quarters

explanation.surface: Soldiers crammed into hot, airless lodgings find themselves uncomfortably near each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a cramped position very near someone, too near for comfort, as in fighting hand to hand.

clue.text: Solicits for votes in the corridors of power?

definitions.meaning: to press legislators for support on a cause is to canvass them in this way
the halls of Parliament where members meet the public are its antechambers

explanation.surface: Campaigners canvass for support in the halls of government.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means pressing politicians for support; as a noun, the entrance halls of a parliament where such pressing happens.

clue.text: Quick, look right inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the abbreviation for right sits within the word for look

parts.note: to look closely is to spy

explanation.surface: An instruction to glance quickly to the right while indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry is a synonym for nimble or lively, quick on one's feet.

clue.text: Meet the requirements and make a reservation

definitions.meaning: to pass the standard needed for something, like an exam or a race
to add a limiting condition to a statement, hedging it

explanation.surface: Someone who meets the conditions for something and books a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reservation' looks like booking a table, but here it is a hedge or proviso added to a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to be eligible and to limit a statement with a condition or reservation.

clue.text: Girl able to turn up on a whole lot of dates

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word for able is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to be able is to be capable, so can

explanation.surface: A girl capable of arriving for many romantic dates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dates' suggests romance but means calendar days; in a down clue 'to turn up' reads the word for able upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly calendar listing many dates with events and data.

clue.text: Two similar bits of tulle for a ballet skirt

indicators.note: two similar items means the same fragment is used twice in a row
bits of tulle points to a fragment taken from that word, its opening pair of letters

explanation.surface: A dancer's skirt made from two matching pieces of fine net fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits of' takes TU, the start of 'tulle', and 'Two similar' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff net skirt worn by ballerinas.

clue.text: Specialist in stock-taking?

parts.note: stock here is livestock, and taking it means stealing cattle, so this is an expert cattle thief rather than an inventory clerk

explanation.surface: An expert at doing a shop's inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock-taking suggests counting goods in a warehouse; read literally it is taking stock, that is stealing cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler is someone who steals cattle or horses, literally a taker of livestock.

clue.text: Ablest recruit transferred to warship

indicators.note: transferred means the letters of the two words are moved into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The most capable new sailor is posted to a fighting ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A battlecruiser is a large, fast, heavily gunned type of warship.

clue.text: It was frightful, as a rule

definitions.text: It was frightful, as a rule

parts.words: It was frightful, as a rule
parts.note: rule here means a period of government, so this was a terrifying regime, not something generally frightful

explanation.surface: Something that was usually frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' seems to mean usually; it means as a period of rule, the bloody phase of the French Revolution of 1793-94.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the period of the French Revolution marked by mass executions, a rule of terror.

clue.text: A pound fixed rate in Canadian place

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight, from Latin libra

indicators.note: fixed means the letters of the word rate are repaired into a new order

explanation.surface: A fixed exchange rate for the pound somewhere in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' suggests money but gives LB, the weight; 'fixed' turns RATE into ERTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is a western province of Canada.

clue.text: Painter out in sea-mist

indicators.note: out signals the letters of sea-mist are put out of order

explanation.surface: An artist lost in coastal fog.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, leader of the Fauvists.

clue.text: I left to start work

indicators.note: start tells us the word to comes first, at the start of the answer

explanation.surface: Someone saying they departed in order to begin their job.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil is to work hard and long, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Furnaces where links can be forged

indicators.note: forged suggests reshaping, so the letters of links are hammered into a new order

explanation.surface: Ovens in which chain links are made.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilns are furnaces or ovens for firing pottery or drying materials.

clue.text: Live ammunition?

parts.note: a living creature that shares its name with a bullet, a pun on live rounds

explanation.surface: Real bullets, as opposed to blanks.
explanation.walkthrough: Live ammunition means real rounds; here it is a living thing whose name also means a bullet, the garden mollusc.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is both a slimy garden creature and a bullet, so it is literally live ammunition.

clue.text: Number get a fever that's ill-defined

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number
ague is an old word for a fever with shivering, such as malaria

explanation.surface: Many people catch a fever whose symptoms are unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: Vague means indistinct or unclear, a synonym for ill-defined.

clue.text: Be on a wild binge

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of be on a run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An urging to go on a riotous drinking spree.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a noisy party or spree, a binge.

clue.text: Blissful state of cats? Yes, if groomed

indicators.note: grooming tidies and rearranges, so the letters of cats and yes are reordered

explanation.surface: Are cats happiest when they are being brushed? Yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is a state of overwhelming happiness, bliss.

clue.text: Final word of encouragement I love

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of encouragement
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone saying a last encouraging word to a loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal British goodbye, the last word said on parting.

clue.text: He doesn't want others to bother him about tortuous clues

definitions.text: He doesn't want others to bother him

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: tortuous means twisted, so the letters of clues are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A solver who wants no help with a set of devious crossword clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse is a person who lives alone and avoids company.

clue.text: Song that once charmed Ulysses

definitions.meaning: a Caribbean style of song, originally from Trinidad
in Greek myth a sea nymph kept Ulysses (Odysseus) on her island for seven years

explanation.surface: A song that bewitched the hero of an ancient epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song' suggests the Sirens, but the nymph of Homer's Odyssey is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a West Indian song style and the nymph who detained Odysseus.

clue.text: Dope and sex orgy gets uncovered

indicators.note: an orgy is wild and disorderly, so the letters of dope and sex are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A drugs and sex party is revealed by reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means laid bare or revealed, the same as uncovered.

clue.text: Drink container — one included in new changes on tax

indicators.note: included in tells us the letter for one is placed within the rearranged word
changes means the letters of new are reordered

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
VAT is value added tax, a sales tax in the UK

explanation.surface: A drinks vessel, with new alterations to the duty on alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges the three letters of 'new' so that, with one inside, they spell a drink; 'on' simply sets the tax after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine vat is a large tank in which wine is made or stored.

clue.text: Point to barrel-shaped singer

parts.note: W, west, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: shaped means the letters of barrel are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A rotund vocalist with a figure like a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrel-shaped' reads as one portly description, but the hyphen hides a split: 'shaped' is the anagram signal working on 'barrel'.
explanation.definitionFit: A warbler is a small songbird, and the word also means any singer who trills.

clue.text: A burning issue may arise from it

definitions.text: A burning issue may arise from it

parts.words: A burning issue may arise from it
parts.note: issue is read literally as something that comes out, here molten lava, rather than a topic of debate

explanation.surface: The source of a hot political topic.
explanation.walkthrough: A burning issue is usually an urgent topic; here it is lava pouring out of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano is a vent from which molten rock, literally burning matter, issues forth.

clue.text: Out of work, one gets led astray

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: astray means gone wrong, so the letters of led wander into a new order

explanation.surface: An unemployed person is led into bad ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means not working, unemployed or inactive.

clue.text: Aside given to an actor to speak?

definitions.meaning: aside as an adverb means to one side or separately

definitions.text: given to an actor to speak?
definitions.meaning: an actor is handed a role, lines to speak

explanation.surface: An aside handed to a stage performer to deliver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aside' looks like the theatrical noun; it is the adverb, as in setting something apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means separately or to one side; split, it is a role handed to an actor.

clue.text: A slight mark on the music

definitions.meaning: a slight is an insult, a disparaging remark
a curved line over notes showing they are played smoothly together

explanation.surface: A small blot on the sheet music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slight' seems an adjective for small; it is a noun meaning an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Slur means an insult, and also the musical sign binding notes into one smooth phrase.

clue.text: Bloomer in which a pupil is to be found

definitions.meaning: a bloomer here is literally a flowering plant, not a blunder

definitions.text: in which a pupil is to be found
definitions.meaning: the coloured ring of the eye surrounds the pupil

explanation.surface: A mistake made by a schoolchild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder and 'pupil' a schoolchild; they are a flower and the eye's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a flower and also the coloured part of the eye around the pupil.

clue.text: Time to come up for discharge

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word time is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: The moment arrives for someone to be released from service.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to give off or send out, a synonym for discharge as a verb.

clue.text: They get taken in by foreigners

definitions.text: They get taken in by foreigners

parts.words: They get taken in by foreigners
parts.note: taken in suggests being deceived; read literally it is goods brought into other countries

explanation.surface: Gullible people who are fooled by visitors from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' looks like conned; it means received, as goods sold abroad are imported by foreign buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: Exports are goods sent abroad, which foreign countries take in.

clue.text: A gumboil no one treated leads to complaint

indicators.note: treated, as by a doctor, means the remaining letters are reworked into a new order
no one tells us the letter for one is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An untreated abscess on the gum leads to further illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no one' removes I from AGUMBOIL, and 'treated' rearranges AGUMBOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is back pain, and a complaint is an everyday word for an ailment.

clue.text: Reward of mature reflection

definitions.meaning: a payment or recompense, as in a small sum for one's trouble
careful thought given to something over time

explanation.surface: The prize that comes from careful thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a payment for a service and careful thought.
